chapter: Family band and learning to play
title: Lonnie Johnson comes to McKinney and needs a band
summary: Tate describes Lonnie Johnson's ups and downs and the night his band failed to show at his aunt's ballroom in McKinney, Texas.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: -- and who else? Ted Weems. Ted Weems had a good swing band during those days and we listened to all the bands, white and black. If they did something we liked, we did it. Then, as I say, we'd learn it, you know, like off the record and we'd play it for our band. One time -- another thing that helped influence me, helped me to make up our mind, Lonnie Johnson -- I know you know the name -- he'd been big many, many times up and down, up and down, he was an amazing man. I've seen Lonnie -- I want to say this before I get into how he influenced me -- I've seen Lonnie when he's riding high with a big record and the next couple of years, I'd see him a bellboy and he always would be the same. He'd be just as jolly and just as happy being the bellboy with a red jacket on as he was when he had diamonds and things on his fingers. He was really that kind of guy.

So he came to McKinney, Texas, which is between -- halfway between Sherman and Dallas and when one of his records was riding high to play in my auntie's ballroom, which we had never played for her, you know. Heavier names had played for her than we were, you know. So the band didn't show. About 6:00 -- he came early that afternoon and the band, about 6:30, 7:00, no band. So -- and he was going to start playing like from nine to twelve. At 12:00, all dances are over then. So he went to my auntie, he says, "Have you any musicians here?" He says, "I think I'm in trouble." He says, "I don't think that band's going to show from Dallas." He says, "I'm pretty sure if they were coming, they would have been here now." So she says, "No, no musicians here." He says, "Well, do you know any near here?" And I don't know why she didn't think of us right off the bat. So she says, "No. Oh," she says, "wait a minute." She says, "I've got some nephews and some cousins up the road." She was in McKinney, that's Herb's home, too, you know, Herb Ellis.

So he said -- he asked her, he said, "Well, can they play?" She said, "They say -- I understand -- people say they sound pretty good." She said, "They look good. Everytime they get some money, they buy a uniform." We got that from Trent, you know. We's sharp.
